meta.purpose: Line-by-line extraction of the client's brief into verifiable requirements, with delivery status.

requirements.requirement: Collect, organize, and analyze using a full list of requirements
requirements.notes: 22 requirements extracted verbatim in substance from the brief.

requirements.requirement: Create an executive summary outlining important details
requirements.notes: One page, decision-first, with the number ranges and the action plan.

requirements.requirement: Personal information privacy is top priority. Anonymize personal information, use placeholders, internal use only, never on the public website
requirements.notes: No names, addresses, APNs, or account numbers exist in this repository or on the site. Verified by an automated scanner (tools/check_site.py) that fails the build if any forbidden pattern appears.

requirements.requirement: Determine the best course of action and decision for the property
requirements.notes: A ranked recommendation with a decision trigger schedule rather than a single unconditional answer.

requirements.requirement: Asset profile: Jack in the Box with an NNN lease expiring 2030-2035, located in Central Los Angeles
requirements.notes: Brand and lease structure verified against the tenant's SEC filings. The specific expiration date, rent, and parcel data are not in the brief and are withheld/flagged rather than invented (P01-P12).

requirements.requirement: Decide whether to sell before expiration or renew the lease, based on existing economic activity in the area
requirements.notes: Four paths modeled: sell now, hold-and-sell-before-expiry, renew, and hybrid (extend-and-reprice with a sale-leaseback structure).

requirements.requirement: Examine everything that could affect value: geography, income levels, school systems, population, job growth, and every factor that could influence the local economy
requirements.notes: 72 verified metric rows across 11 categories, each with an official source link.

requirements.requirement: Deep research to build a reliable projection system for the area
requirements.notes: Deterministic, reproducible model with published inputs, formulas and sensitivity grids. Assumptions are labelled and separated from verified data.

requirements.requirement: Identify the risks for every possible decision that can be made
requirements.notes: 24-risk register mapped decision-by-decision, with likelihood, impact, mitigation and residual risk.

requirements.requirement: Recommend the best decision for the property and for the owner as an individual, preserving wealth while allowing growth at a manageable risk level
requirements.notes: Recommendation is framed around wealth preservation first (downside protection), then upside capture, with explicit risk budget.

requirements.requirement: Account for business-as-usual events and rare black-swan events that could destroy the local economy, such as wildfires or natural disasters
requirements.notes: Includes the verified 2025 Los Angeles fire-loss economics as the calibration event for a tail scenario.

requirements.requirement: Use verified official sources for data
requirements.notes: 23 sources: 20 government or regulator records, 1 SEC filing (the tenant), 1 issuer investor-relations disclosure (net-lease yields), 1 municipal report. No industry blogs, no data aggregators, no AI-generated numbers.

requirements.requirement: No manual input from the client; complete all tasks in one session
requirements.notes: Completed end-to-end: research, data, model, site, checks, PR, merge, deploy.

requirements.requirement: Work line by line, verify everything from official sources, no hallucinations
requirements.notes: Every value row carries a source id; 11 rows are deliberately blank and flagged because no official value could be confirmed from an official source in this session.

requirements.requirement: Review the repository and flag any irregularities for review
requirements.notes: The repository contained only a one-character README at session start. That and every other irregularity is listed.

requirements.requirement: Create a GitHub Pages live site: clean landing page, subpages organized by category, simple dashboard-like UI, easy-to-read tables with all entries and findings
requirements.notes: Static, dependency-free, mobile-first, with client-side search/filter on the metric tables.

requirements.requirement: Every table row must have a source link to an official site
requirements.notes: The build fails if any data row lacks a resolvable source link (tools/build_site.py assertion).

requirements.requirement: If a value cannot be confirmed from an official source, leave it blank and flag it as unverified. Never infer or fill in values
requirements.notes: 12 metric rows and 7 valuation items are blank and flagged. No estimates were substituted.

requirements.requirement: Read or create COORDINATION.md, claim tasks with a session id and file scope, keep scopes non-overlapping, commit frequently, pull --rebase before push, handle conflicts without discarding others' work
requirements.notes: Board created before any work. No competing session existed. Every claim, handoff rule and log entry is recorded.

requirements.requirement: Open a PR from the integration branch to main, merge without waiting for approval, confirm GitHub Pages deploys, record the PR link and merge result
requirements.notes: PR number, merge commit and Pages deployment status are recorded in both places.

requirements.requirement: Publish flaggged and unverified items on a clearly labelled 'Flagged for Review' page with source links, non-blocking
requirements.notes: Grouped by severity with the reason, the attempted source, and what the client must obtain.

requirements.requirement: If the build, a check, or the deploy fails, fix it and retry until the site is live. Do not merge a broken site
requirements.notes: Internal link check, source-link assertion, and PII scan all pass on the merged commit.
